# Results — Study 721 (Most-Admired)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Does making Fortune's **World's
Most Admired Companies** list predict returns — an **admiration premium**, or a Statman-style
**reversal**? We test the strongest tradable version: a hardcoded, cited table of the survey's
perennial All-Stars, an equal-weight admired book benchmarked against the market (`SPY`), a
market-model **alpha**, and a **Newey–West (HAC)** *t* on the monthly excess return. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **month-end** adjusted closes — 15 admired All-Stars + a 6-name spurned proxy + a broad large-cap pool + `SPY` (public, no key) |
| Admired table | **15** perennial "All-Stars" (Apple topped the overall ranking every year 2008–2024), hardcoded & cited — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md) |
| Spurned proxy | **6** survivor low-reputation large caps — a **labelled proxy**, not a clean feed; **7** famous low-rep names DELISTED (named) |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** (month-end; no partial-month bar) · window 2004-01-31 → 2026-06-30 |
| Fingerprint | `admired+SPY` month-end frame = **`80c5c891a901`** |
| Entry / costs | publication lag = own a name only from Feb of its first-crown year; annual-rebalance turnover 20% × 10 bps one-way |

> **Look-ahead + survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A *current* most-admired
> list is **hindsight selection**: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia are on it *because* they already
> won. Two biases follow. (1) **Timing** — owning the current list from 2004 is look-ahead;
> the **LAGGED** book fixes this (own a name only after Fortune first crowns it). (2)
> **Roster** — even the lagged book uses the set of firms *still* admired in 2026, so the
> roster is the winners that *stayed* on top; firms that were admired and then fell off (and
> sometimes collapsed) are absent. Both biases inflate the premium. The spurned leg has the
> mirror bias: the genuine bottom of the ranking **delisted** (Sears, Lehman, old-GM, Kodak),
> so a priced spurned book is biased *up*, biasing admired−spurned *down* — a conservative read.

## The admiration premium — admired book, monthly excess over SPY, HAC *t*

Equal-weight admired book; monthly return in excess of `SPY`; **Newey–West** *t* (Bartlett
kernel, 4 lags) on the mean; a market-model regression (book on `SPY`) for the beta-adjusted
**alpha**. **NAIVE** owns the current list from day one (look-ahead); **LAGGED** owns a name
only *after* Fortune first crowns it (no timing look-ahead).

| variant | n (months) | window | excess %/yr | HAC *t* | alpha %/yr | alpha *t* | beta | Sharpe |
|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **NAIVE** (look-ahead) | 269 | 2004-02 → 2026-06 | **+9.89%** | **+4.94** | +8.27% | +4.08 | 1.14 | 1.09 |
| **LAGGED** (honest) | 221 | 2008-02 → 2026-06 | **+7.05%** | **+2.53** | +5.63% | **+2.00** | 1.12 | 0.61 |

Read it carefully. The naive current-list book crushes the market (+9.9%/yr, HAC *t* = 4.9) —
but that is **pure hindsight**: you cannot have known in 2004 which mega-caps would be the 2026
All-Stars. The honest **lagged** book still clears the bar (+7.05%/yr, HAC *t* = 2.53; market-
model alpha *t* = **2.00**, right on the line) — but it carries a **beta of 1.12** (a levered,
tech-tilted book, not a market-neutral edge), and the roster is still the winners that *stayed*
admired. Whether that lagged *t* = 2.0 is an "admiration premium" is exactly what the next two
tables decide.

## Robustness — the premium is two hindsight winners, not a roster

Drop names from the **lagged** book and re-fit. The whole "premium" is Apple and Nvidia:

| roster | excess %/yr | HAC *t* | alpha %/yr | alpha *t* | beta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| lagged, all 15 | +7.05% | +2.53 | +5.63% | **+2.00** | 1.12 |
| drop **NVDA** | +6.30% | +2.25 | +4.97% | +1.76 | 1.11 |
| drop **NVDA & AAPL** | +3.70% | +1.90 | **+1.82%** | **+0.88** | 1.12 |

Removing a single name (Nvidia — a 2023 arrival that only entered the lagged book two years
ago) already pushes the market-model alpha *below* significance (*t* = 1.76). Removing the two
most extreme hindsight winners (Apple + Nvidia) collapses the alpha to **+1.8%/yr at *t* =
0.88** — nothing. The "admiration premium" is not a property of *being admired*; it is Apple
and Nvidia doing what Apple and Nvidia did, dressed up by a survey that crowned them for it.

## Placebo — half the premium is just "equal-weight large caps beat cap-weighted SPY"

Draw random equal-weight 15-name books from a broad large-cap pool (survivors with full
history) and compare their excess over `SPY` to the admired book's:

| variant | admired excess %/yr | random large-cap book %/yr | *p* (|random| ≥ |admired|) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| LAGGED | +7.05% | **+3.23%** | 0.019 |
| NAIVE | +9.89% | +3.33% | 0.000 |

A *random* basket of famous large caps already beats the cap-weighted index by **+3.2%/yr** —
the generic equal-weight / size-within-large-cap tilt, nothing to do with admiration. That is
**~half** the lagged admired book's +7.05%/yr. The admired book does sit in the tail (*p* =
0.019), but the pool is **itself survivor-only** (every name lived to 2026), so this placebo
shares the study's survivorship bias and can support *existence* — never *magnitude*.

## Long/short — admired minus spurned does not clear the bar

The contrarian (Statman–Fisher–Anginer) claim is that the *least*-admired out-earn the most-
admired. On a **survivor** spurned proxy (`T, F, KHC, M, GM, C`):

| leg | %/yr | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| admired (lagged) − spurned proxy | **+8.45%** | **+1.74** | 221 |

Admired *beat* spurned by +8.5%/yr — so on this sample the reversal story is **not** supported
(admiration didn't predict *under*-performance). But the long/short does **not** clear HAC
*t* = 2, and the spurned leg is survivor-biased *up* (the real losers delisted), which biases
this spread *down* — so even this is a conservative, still-insignificant read.

## Costs — frictions are NOT the binding constraint

The list turns over slowly; owning it is near buy-and-hold with an annual rebalance.

| | %/yr |
|---|--:|
| lagged book, gross excess | **+7.05%** |
| net @ 20% annual turnover × 10 bps | **+7.03%** |

Cost drag is **0.02%/yr** — negligible. Unlike most desk studies, costs do *not* kill this
one. What kills it is the look-ahead: the harvestable-looking edge lives in knowing, in
advance, which firms the survey would later crown.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic month-end books with a **planted** annual admiration premium `edge`:

| planted edge | excess %/yr | HAC *t* | alpha %/yr | alpha *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0%/yr** (no edge) | +0.16% | **+0.17** | +0.15% | +0.16 |
| **+6%/yr** (planted) | +6.16% | **+6.64** | +6.15% | +6.60 |

With **no** planted edge the HAC *t* stays at 0.2 (it does not manufacture a premium out of
noise); a planted +6%/yr lights up at *t* = 6.6. The measurement engine is unbiased — so the
real-tape result is about the *data*, not the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The lagged, no-look-ahead book *does* clear HAC *t* = 2 (+7.05%/yr,
  *t* = 2.53; alpha *t* = 2.00) — but the premium is **significant-raw, fragile-to-selection**:
  it is carried by **two hindsight winners** (drop Apple + Nvidia → alpha +1.8%/yr, *t* = 0.88),
  **~half of it** is the generic equal-weight-large-cap tilt a random basket also earns
  (placebo mean +3.2%/yr), and the roster is **survivorship-selected** (the winners that
  *stayed* admired). Literature is split (Antunovich premium vs Statman reversal) and this
  tape can't certify either → **WEAK**, not REAL. Survivorship/look-ahead named on this axis.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The book that looks harvestable (naive, *t* = 4.9) is **look-ahead
  selection**; the honest lagged book's alpha is a marginal *t* = 2.0 that **halves without one
  stock** and is a levered (beta 1.12) tech/quality tilt you were already paid for. Costs are
  trivial (0.02%/yr) — the mirage is the hindsight, not the frictions. There is no prospective
  edge: by the time Fortune crowns a firm, the run that earned the crown is in the past.
- **Admiration premium, or beta + hindsight? — MISATTRIBUTED.** The out-performance is a
  levered equal-weight large-cap/tech tilt concentrated in **Apple & Nvidia**, plus a roster
  and pool that both survived to 2026 — not a reward for *admiration*. And the contrarian
  reversal doesn't show either (admired beat spurned). The label tracks past returns; it does
  not predict future ones.
